extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / readers of Mochizuki's IUT theory
extracted.subtask_description: Formal constructions and compatibility conditions for monoids, semi-simplifications, theta/gaussian monoids, symmetrizing isomorphisms, and Frobenioids in the setting of Θ- and D-Θell-Hodge theaters in Mochizuki's IUT theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant Monoids (Prop. 4.4 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kummer structure κ†v : O(†Cv) → A†Dv together with the tautological equality †Dv = †Uv determine a unique isomorphism Ψ†F_v ∼→ Ψcns(†Uv) of topological monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a uniqueness assertion: the Kummer-theoretic data determine the constant (cns) monoid assignment and a canonical identification; implicit caveat: constructions are up to the usual conjugacy indeterminacies referenced elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic Semi-simplifications (Prop. 4.4 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a unique {±1}-orbit of isomorphisms of topological groups Ψ×†F_v ∼→ Ψcns(†D_v)× and a unique isomorphism of monoids ΨR†F_v ∼→ ΨR_cns(†D_v) = R≥0(†D_v) mapping the distinguished element (nat-ural logarithm element giving pv = e) to the distinguished element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yields a natural poly-isomorphism between the semi-simplified versions Ψss†F_v ∼→ Ψss_cns(†D_v); compatibility with natural splittings is required. Emphasizes distinguished element normalization (pv = e = 2.71828...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels, F±-Symmetries, and Conjugate Synchronization (Prop. 4.4 (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The isomorphism of (i) determines, for each t ∈ LabCusp±(†Uv), compatible isomorphisms l(Ψ†F)_t_v ∼→ Ψcns(†Uv)_t and F±-symmetrizing isomorphisms (induced by F± actions) between data indexed by distinct labels; these symmetrizing isomorphisms determine diagonal submonoids and an isomorphism of topological monoids l(Ψ†F)_0_v ∼→ (Ψ†F)_l_v/†Ucor_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the existence and compatibility of symmetrizing isomorphisms relating labeled local data, and their role in forming diagonal submonoids; references conjugate synchronization as a key property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta and Gaussian Monoids (Prop. 4.4 (iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and formal evaluation isomorphisms produce natural isomorphisms Ψ†FΘ_v ∼→ Ψenv(†Uv) ∼→ Ψgau(†Uv) ∼→ ΨFgau(†F_v), which restrict to the identity or to the (−)× restriction of the isomorphisms of (i) on copies of Ψ× and are compatible with natural splittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes existence of theta and gaussian monoids and their mutual evaluation isomorphisms, compatibility with splittings, and restrictions to unit components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial algorithm for Constant Monoids (Cor. 4.5 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial algorithm in a D-prime-strip ‡D for constructing the assignment Ψcns(‡D) with values Ψcns(‡D)_v defined by formulas differing on Vnon and Varc, where bracketed data are well-defined only up to ‡Πv-conjugacy indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction is functorial but only determined up to conjugacy indeterminacy in local factors; references prior propositions for justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Mono-analytic Semi-simplifications and Frobenioid construction (Cor. 4.5 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A functorial algorithm in the D(cid:3)-prime-strip ‡D(cid:3) constructs Ψss_cns(‡D(cid:3))_v with splittings Ψss = Ψss_× × R≥0 and distinguished elements log(pv) ∈ R≥0; produces a Frobenioid D(cid:3)(‡D(cid:3)) isomorphic to an indicated Frobenioid and a bijection Prime(D(cid:3)(‡D(...))) ∼→ V, together with isomorphisms of divisor-submonoids ΦD(...)_v ∼→ R≥0(‡D(...)_v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the splitting into unit and non-unit parts, distinguished elements on the R≥0 components, conjugacy indeterminacies, and a canonical Frobenioid realization with Prime bijection to V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Labels and F±-Symmetries (Cor. 4.5 (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a bijection ζ, local F±-actions induce symmetrizing isomorphisms between labeled data Ψcns(†D)_t for distinct t in LabCusp±(†D); these glue compatibly to give diagonal submonoids and a global isomorphism Ψcns(†D)_0 ∼→ Ψcns(†D)(...)F_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how local symmetries assemble to global symmetries via bijections of labels and how diagonal (global) structures are obtained; compatibility with earlier local constructions is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Theta and Gaussian Monoids algorithm (Cor. 4.5 (iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial algorithm in the D-prime-strip †D for constructing assignments Ψenv(†D)_v, Ψgau(†D)_v and their ∞-variants, equipped with topological group actions when v ∈ Vnon and splittings for all v, together with compatible evaluation isomorphisms Ψenv(†D) ∼→ Ψgau(†D) and their ∞-versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local data carry actions by topological groups at non-archimedean v and splittings at all v; evaluation isomorphisms relate envelope and gaussian monoids; references to Corollary 3.5 and earlier propositions for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Realiﬁed Theta and Gaussian Frobenioids (Cor. 4.5 (v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A functorial algorithm in the D(cid:3)-prime-strip constructs a reified Frobenioid D(cid:3)_env (realified quotient by units with formal log symbol) and a subcategory D(cid:3)_gau thought of as a 'weighted diagonal' with divisor and rational function monoids determined by a vector of ratios indexed by j ∈ F_2^l; for each v an isomorphism ΦD(...)_v ∼→ Ψenv(...)_v^R (resp. for gau) is produced and a global formal evaluation isomorphism of Frobenioids D_env ∼→ D_gau compatible with local evaluation isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction involves reification (quotienting by units), weighted diagonal structures determined by specified weights j^2, and compatibility of global Frobenioid isomorphisms with local data; references technical conventions and earlier propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenioid-theoretic vs monoid-theoretic formulations (Remark 4.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: One may reinterpret constructed collections of monoids as Frobenioids; Frobenioid formulations are technically easier when associated Picard groups contain nontorsion elements (i.e., when degree of line bundles is nontrivial); but Frobenioid formulations are less suited for conjugate synchronization discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on which formalism is more convenient: use Frobenioid-theoretic descriptions for global arithmetic Frobenioids and when Pic has nontorsion, but remain cautious for conjugate synchronization contexts where monoid descriptions may be preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeled semi-simplifications and multi-basepoint variants (Remark 4.5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Symmetrizing isomorphisms analogous to Cor. 4.5 (iii) can be constructed for labeled semi-simplifications and for global reified Frobenioids; multi-basepoint versions (passing to D-Θell-bridges or capsules/processions) are also available, with routine details left to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes existence of labeled and multi-basepoint variants; indicates routine nature but references IUTchI propositions for the constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of F_3^±-symmetry for Conjugate Synchronization (Remark 4.5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate synchronization in Cor. 3.5 and 4.5 is possible for F_3^±-symmetry due to connectedness of local components at each v and the 'geometric' nature of automorphisms; the global portion †D^± is necessary to synchronize local ±-indeterminacies, producing profinite conjugacy indeterminacies (Δ-conjugacy) in earlier corollaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why certain symmetry (F_3^±) allows conjugate synchronization while F_2^l does not, and why global data are required; ties to the need for complements on tempered coverings in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial construction of Ψcns(‡F) from F-prime-strip (Cor. 4.6 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A functorial algorithm in an F-prime-strip ‡F produces Ψcns(‡F)_v (with formulas depending on Vnon vs Varc), well-defined only up to ‡Πv-conjugacy indeterminacy; there are Kummer-theoretic isomorphisms Ψcns(‡F) ∼→ Ψcns(‡D) determined by prior propositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel to D-prime-strip constant monoids but in F-prime-strip context; emphasizes conjugacy indeterminacies and reliance on Kummer-theoretic identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: F-prime-strip Mono-analytic Semi-simplifications and Frobenioid iso (Cor. 4.6 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A functorial algorithm in the F(cid:3)-prime-strip constructs Ψss_cns(‡F(cid:3))_v (with splittings and distinguished elements) and yields an isomorphism of Frobenioids ‡C(cid:3) ∼→ D(cid:3)(‡D(cid:3)) uniquely determined by compatibility with Prime(−) bijections and local isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights need to construct both Ψss and compatible global Frobenioid isomorphism; conjugacy indeterminacies at v∈Vnon are independent of label t.

rubrics_metrics.name: F-prime-strip Labels and F±-Symmetries (Cor. 4.6 (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection of isomorphisms of (i) determines, for each t ∈ LabCusp±(†D), compatible isomorphisms Ψcns(†F)_t ∼→ Ψcns(†D)_t and F±-symmetrizing isomorphisms between data indexed by distinct t; these glue to give diagonal submonoids and a global isomorphism Ψcns(†F)_0 ∼→ Ψcns(†F)(...)F_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to Cor. 4.5 (iii) but in F-prime-strip setting; stresses label-compatibility and independence of certain conjugacy indeterminacies from t.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-bridge Local Theta/Gaussian constructions (Cor. 4.6 (iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a Θ-bridge glued to the Θ±-bridge, there is a functorial algorithm for constructing ΨFenv(†HT Θ)_v, ΨFgau(†HT Θ)_v and ∞-variants, equipped with topological group actions at v∈Vnon and splittings for all v, and with evaluation isomorphisms relating these to Ψenv(†D>) and Ψgau(†D>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses the gluing algorithm from IUTchI Proposition 6.7; local/global compatibilities and evaluation isomorphisms mirror earlier constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global realified Frobenioid constructions in Θ-bridge (Cor. 4.6 (v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying the isomorphism ‡C(cid:3) ∼→ D(cid:3)(‡D(cid:3)) to global Frobenioids of Cor. 4.5 yields functorial algorithms producing Frobenioids C_env(†HT Θ), C_gau(†HT Θ) with bijections Prime(−)∼→ V and isomorphisms ΦC_env,v ∼→ ΨFenvR_v, ΦC_gau,v ∼→ ΨFgauR_v; evaluation isomorphisms conjugate the Cor. 4.5 evaluation via these identifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details the passage from local to global Frobenioid constructions tied to Θ-bridges and the compatibility of evaluation isomorphisms after conjugation by global identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstructibility of distinguished elements (Remark 4.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ Vnon the poly-isomorphism Ψss_cns(†Gv) can be algorithmically reconstructed from †F(cid:3)_v; for v ∈ Varc the non-unit portion / distinguished element of Ψss†F_v cannot be reconstructed algorithmically from †F(cid:3)_v alone, but can be computed from distinguished elements at Vnon together with global Frobenioid structure when ‡C and D(...) are reconstructed compatibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies a practical limitation: archimedean (Varc) distinguished elements require global currency-exchange data (global Frobenioids) to compute; gives the metaphor of global Frobenioids as 'devices for currency exchange' among local divisor monoids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-realiﬁed Global Structures (Cor. 4.7 (i))
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial algorithm in the category †D(cid:6) constructing a morphism †D(cid:6) → †D(cid:7), associated monoid/field/pseudo-monoid objects with π1(†D(cid:7))- / πrat / πκ-sol actions and corresponding Frobenioids F(mod)(†D(cid:6)) etc., together with the natural realification functor to realified Frobenioids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how non‑reified global monoid/field/pseudo-monoid data and their Frobenioids are constructed functorially with group actions and how they relate via a realification functor; references IUTchI example for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels and F2_l-Symmetry (Cor. 4.7 (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a bijection ζ: LabCusp(†D(cid:6)) ∼→ J ∼→ F_2^l, functorial algorithms construct F-prime-strips F(6)(†D)|_j (well-defined up to isomorphism) and the poly-action of F_2^l induces F_2^l-symmetrizing isomorphisms between labeled data for distinct j; these determine diagonal F-prime-strips/submonoids/subrings/sub-pseudo-monoids and subcategories as formal diagonal constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how the F_2^l global symmetry yields labeled isomorphisms and diagonalized global objects; emphasizes the formal notational nature of 'diagonal' constructions and independent conjugacy indeterminacies for distinct j.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization functors and realified global structures (Cor. 4.7 (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For j ∈ LabCusp(†D(cid:6)) there are functorial localization functors/poly-morphisms from global Frobenioids and monoid objects to localized versions (realified), natural isomorphisms D(cid:3)(†D(cid:3)_j) ∼→ F(7)R_mod(†D(cid:6))_j, and for each v an isomorphism R≥0(†D(cid:3)_j)_v ∼→ Ψ(F(4)(†D(4))|_j)^R,v; all compatible with F_2^l-symmetrizing isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the recipe for passing from global to local (and realified) structures and ensuring compatibility of local divisor monoids with the Frobenioid picture; references Example 5.4 of IUTchI for the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel applicability of F_3^± symmetrizing observations to F_2^l case (Remark 4.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations about F_3^±-symmetrizing isomorphisms (e.g., in Cor. 4.5 (iii)) carry over to the F_2^l-symmetrizing isomorphisms of Cor. 4.7 (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that analogous structural remarks and compatibility properties apply across the two symmetry settings; acts as a cross-reference reminder to earlier remarks.
